task: Core 1186 U10A navigation authority scope classification

assuranceCeiling.rationale: These two canonical authorities must classify the same existing admin-navigation files before any #1186 product edit. The work changes only risk and Atlas ownership metadata plus regression coverage; it does not change tenant entitlements, SQL, route guards, operational permissions or production. Guard, semantic scope, replay, CI, Truth and lifecycle closure remain mandatory.

acceptanceCriteria: The canonical DOMAIN-ADMIN maps src/lib/navigation/admin-ia.ts and src/lib/navigation/entitlement-navigation.ts to the existing admin-operations owner without adding a parallel navigation authority.
The canonical release risk policy classifies those same two paths under existing medium-risk admin-operations and does not change any other subsystem risk classification.
The existing navigation behavior, Digital Office Pro route shell, Alap email and support operations, all entitlement grants and all tenant state remain unchanged in this prerequisite release.
A targeted regression proves both files resolve to DOMAIN-ADMIN and the admin-operations risk owner; full required knowledge and development gates complete on the exact SHA.
invariants: Only canonical scope metadata and bounded regression tests change in this unit; product routes, access gates, database objects and tenant records are untouched.
No Pro-only Digital Office functionality becomes available to Alap as a side effect of classification; no new exemptions, aliases or shadow authorization systems are introduced.
The full knowledge-infrastructure known-failure replay stays mandatory because DOMAIN ownership mapping is canonical quality input.
U10A is only a scope prerequisite; it cannot be claimed to close the UI/navigation drift or #1186 overall.
forbiddenStates: Unclassified navigation files are edited as product code before the Development Guard has a stable authority and scope.
A new domain or duplicate entitlement controller is invented instead of extending DOMAIN-ADMIN and admin-operations.
Full quality and failure replay are skipped to force a misleading green result on a knowledge-authority change.

failureModes: The Atlas derives DOMAIN-ADMIN for one file but leaves its companion navigation resolver unowned, allowing unsound scope drift.
A too-broad navigation glob inadvertently classifies storefront-only navigation code as admin security authority.
Changing the policy without a matching domain map leaves the next Development Guard blocked by unresolved architecture scope.
The knowledge-infrastructure change expands known-failure scope to 49 regression records; a partial replay would understate release risk.
A broader policy edit accidentally changes other subsystem risk weights or permits unbounded release changes.
edgeCases: The two navigation files exist but one does not have an Atlas import edge under the expected owner.
Only a test filename changes, yielding vacuous proof without verifying canonical machine-readable classification.
The main branch advances after plan creation, requiring explicit transaction base reconciliation before continuing.
An implementation adds a new navigation entry but never closes route-level permissions; U10A alone must not claim U10 is complete.

alternatives.summary: Extend DOMAIN-ADMIN exact path ownership and admin-operations classification for the two existing admin navigation authority modules.
alternatives.reason: Correctly closes the previously unresolved scope while leaving storefront navigation outside admin and retaining original guard ownership.

alternatives.summary: Patch only an admin-layout visibility branch and leave shared navigation modules outside Atlas classification.
alternatives.reason: Would bypass canonical authorization metadata, duplicate policy locally and violate the mandatory Plan Before Code classification prerequisite.

alternatives.summary: Assign every src/lib/navigation file to the admin domain and risk subsystem with a broad recursive wildcard.
alternatives.reason: Would misclassify storefront navigation and silently expand business authority beyond the observed defect.

specialistReviews.finding: DOMAIN-ADMIN currently owns admin routes and components but not these shared navigation authority modules.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add the two exact files to the existing domain definition and preserve the current domain taxonomy.

specialistReviews.finding: A broad src/lib/navigation wildcard could incorrectly place storefront routing behavior under the admin security owner.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use explicit paths; subsequent U10B must still prove Pro-only route and server authorization independently.

specialistReviews.finding: Changing the canonical domain foundations triggers full knowledge replay while the risk policy itself is release infrastructure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep release risk bounded to the two authority files and require exact-head CI and Truth evidence for this metadata-only release.

challenge.scenario: An Alap tenant can still see a Digital Office link after this scope patch.
challenge.finding: The scope patch intentionally does not change user-visible behavior and must not be reported as the final fix.
challenge.resolution: Keep #1186 open and require the following U10B navigation/runtime proof.

challenge.scenario: A broad wildcard matches storefront navigation files that should not be owned by the admin domain.
challenge.finding: Navigation authority may be incorrectly interpreted as tenant admin authorization.
challenge.resolution: Map only the two already identified merchant admin navigation modules.

challenge.scenario: Only one of the canonical release and domain mappings is updated.
challenge.finding: The next Plan Before Code still sees unresolved owner or subsystem classification.
challenge.resolution: Update both authorities coherently and test both paths in the same regression.

challenge.scenario: A release budget path is accidentally moved from medium to low risk.
challenge.finding: The dependency chain would produce an unsafe release-risk assessment.
challenge.resolution: Preserve existing admin-operations risk and assign exact navigation files to that current medium tier.

challenge.scenario: Knowledge policy modifications incorrectly reuse earlier green QA proof.
challenge.finding: Known failure and Control Plane data products may be stale across the altered architecture registry.
challenge.resolution: Force full incremental replay and exact-head knowledge preflight evidence.

challenge.scenario: Other non-admin navigation files are silently reclassified.
challenge.finding: Unexpected ownership can hide future storefront regressions and break implementation impact routing.
challenge.resolution: Assert the unrelated storefront-ia path is not part of the new admin classification.

proofPlan: Inspect generated Development Guard and Atlas scope reports before any implementation change; require confirmed classification as a prerequisite.
Run Plan Before Code with the exact main transaction base and compare actual planned domain, authority, failure and negative-knowledge sets.
Add regression coverage to the existing Control Plane ecosystem test without editing authorization, runtime routes or grants.
Run edit-time and Reference Sync, Knowledge Preflight and full known-failure Incremental Replay after the coherent authority update.
Run typecheck, quality tests, CI, read-only Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure on the exact resulting commit; do not merge or mark #1186 done from scope metadata alone.

requirements.requirement: Both existing merchant admin navigation modules are deterministically owned by the existing DOMAIN-ADMIN and admin-operations scopes in canonical machine-readable policy without a behavior change.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Navigation ownership must not be bypassed through a broad wildcard, an unrelated domain, or a parallel authorization controller.

notes: Prerequisite governance release for the accepted Core #1186 Digital Office Pro-only entitlement closure. The real main was inspected at the exact declared SHA. Existing U01-U09 changes already reside on main; F35 remains separate draft and is not a base or dependency. No implementation source changes are authorized until canonical Development Guard and Plan Before Code both show PASS on this exact plan; keep this transaction draft otherwise.
